Comic heroes, by first appearance.Tintin: Hergé's reporter, with his dog Snowy, debuted in a Belgian newspaper supplement in January 1929. Tintin has been translated into over 70 languages.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.The Phantom: Lee Falk's 'Ghost Who Walks' was among the first heroes in a skin-tight costume and mask, years before Superman.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.Superman: The pair who created him, Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster, sold the character to the publisher for $130 in the late 1930s.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.Batman: Bob Kane got the credit for decades, but writer Bill Finger shaped much of the character, and he was officially credited in 2015.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.Wonder Woman: Creator William Moulton Marston also helped invent an early lie detector, and her golden lasso compels truth-telling.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.Asterix: Goscinny and Uderzo's Gaulish warrior has been translated into over 100 languages and dialects, with a French theme park near Paris.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.Spider-Man: Spidey was a teenager with money and homework troubles, something new in a genre of adult heroes. Stan Lee wrote and Steve Ditko drew him.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.Judge Dredd: Dredd made his debut in 2000 AD, the British comic. John Wagner and Carlos Ezquerra created the law enforcer of Mega-City One.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird started the turtles as a black-and-white indie comic that parodied popular superhero tales.
Comic heroes, by first appearance.Sandman (Morpheus): Neil Gaiman's Lord of Dreams starred in a series that, in 1991, became the first comic to win a World Fantasy Award, for a Shakespeare-based issue.

Golf greats, by first major win.Bobby Jones: He won the Grand Slam in 1930 as an amateur, then co-founded Augusta National and the Masters.
Golf greats, by first major win.Ben Hogan: He survived a 1949 car crash, then won six more majors, and in 1953 won three majors in one year.
Golf greats, by first major win.Arnold Palmer: 'The King' won his first Masters in 1958 and helped make golf a TV sport. A drink is named after him.
Golf greats, by first major win.Jack Nicklaus: He won a record 18 majors, and his first, the 1962 US Open, came in a playoff against Arnold Palmer.
Golf greats, by first major win.Tom Watson: He won the 1975 Open at Carnoustie, and in 2009, at nearly 60, almost won it again at Turnberry.
Golf greats, by first major win.Seve Ballesteros: A Spaniard, he won the 1979 Open at 22, and his creativity from the rough fuelled Europe's Ryder Cup resurgence.
Golf greats, by first major win.Nick Faldo: He won the 1987 Open at Muirfield by making 18 straight pars on the final day, and he ended with six majors.
Golf greats, by first major win.Tiger Woods: He won the 1997 Masters by 12 strokes at age 21, the youngest champion there at that time.
Golf greats, by first major win.Phil Mickelson: He won the 2004 Masters after many near misses, and in 2021 became the oldest major champion at 50.
Golf greats, by first major win.Rory McIlroy: He won the 2011 US Open at Congressional by eight strokes, and completed the career Grand Slam at the 2025 Masters.

Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.Pyrex: Corning's heatproof glass began as railroad lantern glass, and a scientist's wife reportedly baked a cake in a cut-off battery jar.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.KitchenAid stand mixer: The brand reportedly got its name when a factory executive's wife said it was the best kitchen aid she had ever had.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.Vitamix: It began as a door-to-door seller of blenders, and modern machines can heat soup just by friction.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.Le Creuset: Each pot is cast in its own sand mold, destroyed after use, and the signature orange color comes from a furnace color.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.Tefal: The French firm first stuck non-stick Teflon onto aluminum pans, and the name blends Teflon and aluminium.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.Amana Radarange microwave: Raytheon's Percy Spencer discovered microwave heating when a chocolate bar melted in his pocket; the first Radarange was as big as a fridge.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.Crock-Pot: Based on an earlier bean cooker, the slow cooker's brand name became a common word for it.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.George Foreman Grill: The boxer's grill has sold well over 100 million units.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.Roomba: Made by a company that previously built military robots, it sold tens of millions of its robot vacuums.
Kitchen brands and gadgets, by debut yea.Instant Pot: A Canadian engineer built this pressure cooker, and its Amazon sales exploded in the 2010s.

Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Heron's coin vending machine: Hero of Alexandria described a device that released a measure of holy water when a coin dropped onto a lever.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Newspaper ad in America: The Boston News-Letter ran it, advertising a Long Island estate for sale and a reward for stolen anvils.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Radio commercial: WEAF in New York aired a ten-minute pitch for apartments in Queens, an early ad paid for by the minute.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.TV commercial (Bulova): Bulova reportedly paid about nine dollars for a ten-second spot before a baseball game in July 1941.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Enclosed mall (Southdale): Designed by Victor Gruen in Minnesota, it was the first fully enclosed, climate-controlled shopping mall in the US.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Cash machine (ATM): Barclays in London installed the first in June 1967; its inventor John Shepherd-Barron said the idea came to him in the bath.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Barcode scanned at checkout: A pack of Wrigley's gum was the first item scanned at a store checkout, in Ohio on 26 June 1974.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Spam email: Gary Thuerk of Digital Equipment sent an ad to hundreds of ARPANET users in 1978, and the angry replies began right away.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Web banner ad: AT&T's banner on HotWired asked, Have you ever clicked your mouse right here? You will. Many people did.
Commerce firsts, from ancient to online.Apple App Store opens: It launched with about 500 apps in July 2008 and now holds millions; the word app became popular around it.

When these famous speeches were given.Elizabeth I at Tilbury: Elizabeth I said at Tilbury that she had the heart and stomach of a king, as the Spanish Armada threatened England.
When these famous speeches were given.Patrick Henry's liberty speech: Patrick Henry's give me liberty or give me death speech is traditionally remembered, though it was reconstructed after his death.
When these famous speeches were given.Gettysburg Address: The Gettysburg Address was only about 270 words and lasted a few minutes, but it redefined the Civil War as a fight for equality.
When these famous speeches were given.FDR: 'Nothing to fear': FDR said the only thing we have to fear is fear itself during his first inauguration, at the depths of the Great Depression.
When these famous speeches were given.Churchill: 'on the beaches': Churchill's we shall fight on the beaches was delivered to Parliament, and it was not broadcast live on the radio at that time.
When these famous speeches were given.Nehru: 'Tryst with Destiny': Nehru gave his Tryst with Destiny speech at midnight as India became independent, and he spoke of the world sleeping while India awakes.
When these famous speeches were given.JFK: 'Ask not': JFK's ask not what your country can do for you came in his inaugural address, and it still defines a generation.
When these famous speeches were given.MLK: 'I Have a Dream': Martin Luther King Jr.'s I Have a Dream speech was delivered at the March on Washington, and the famous dream section was largely improvised.
When these famous speeches were given.Reagan: 'Tear down this wall': Reagan challenged Gorbachev to tear down the Berlin Wall at the Brandenburg Gate, and the Wall fell about two years later.
When these famous speeches were given.Mandela's release speech: Nelson Mandela's release speech was given after 27 years in prison, and he spoke from the Cape Town city hall balcony.

Alcohol by volume of these beers.Berliner Weisse: A tart, low-alcohol wheat beer from Germany, traditionally served with a splash of raspberry or woodruff syrup.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.Guinness Draught: The creamy head comes from nitrogen gas, and its dark color comes from roasted barley, though held to the light it is ruby brown.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.Hefeweizen: This German wheat beer is unfiltered, and yeast gives it banana and clove aromas.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.IPA: Extra hops, a natural preservative, supposedly helped beer survive long ship voyages to British India.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.Belgian Tripel: Made popular by Belgian Trappist monks, this strong, pale ale is hidden under a smooth, fruity taste.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.Barleywine: As strong as wine, this style is brewed to improve in the bottle over years.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.Samuel Adams Utopias: Brewed in tiny batches and aged in barrels, it is served in small glasses like cognac, uncarbonated, and costs hundreds of dollars.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.Tactical Nuclear Penguin: BrewDog made it with freeze distillation, and the Scottish brewery's name was deliberately provocative.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.Sink the Bismarck!: BrewDog released it as an answer to a German brewery's 40 percent beer, naming it after a famous WWII battleship.
Alcohol by volume of these beers.Brewmeister Snake Venom: Despite its name, it contains no snake venom, and its alcohol content is created by freezing and removing ice.

Local time when it's noon in London (in.Honolulu: Hawaii never changes its clocks, so it stays 10 hours behind London in winter, and it is one of the few US places that skips daylight saving.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.Los Angeles: Los Angeles is eight hours behind London, which leaves only a brief window each day when Hollywood and London offices are both at work.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.New York: New York trails London by five hours in winter, so a London lunchtime call catches New Yorkers at the start of their working day.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.Rio de Janeiro: Brazil scrapped daylight saving in 2019, so Rio sits a steady three hours behind London in winter, in the middle of its summer.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.Reykjavik: Iceland sits on Greenwich Mean Time all year and never changes its clocks, so in January its time matches London's exactly.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.Paris: Though much of France lies west of the prime meridian, it uses Central European Time, an hour ahead of London.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.Moscow: Russia dropped seasonal clock changes in 2014 and stayed on permanent winter time, so Moscow runs three hours ahead of London.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.New Delhi: India spans about 30 degrees of longitude yet keeps a single national time, UTC+5:30, whose half-hour offset puzzles many visitors.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.Tokyo: Japan skips daylight saving, and Tokyo stays nine hours ahead of London in winter, so London's noon is Tokyo's evening.
Local time when it's noon in London (in.Sydney: January is high summer in Sydney, which observes daylight saving and runs 11 hours ahead of London, so noon in London is late evening there.

Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㄱ (g): King Sejong the Great created Hangul in 1443, and this letter's shape depicts the tongue at the back of the mouth.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㄷ (d): Its shape is said to trace the tongue touching the ridge behind the upper teeth.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㄹ (r/l): This letter sounds like a quick r at the start of a syllable and an l at the end, and its zigzag shape suggests a curled tongue.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㅁ (m): The square shape imitates the closed lips used to say it.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㅂ (b): It is the first letter of bibimbap, the rice dish whose name means mixed rice.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㅅ (s): The shape is said to depict the teeth, and it begins words like seoul-tae and sa-ram, the word for person.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㅈ (j): It starts the name of Jeju Island, the volcanic holiday island south of the Korean mainland.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㅊ (ch): It is the letter ㅈ with an extra stroke on top, which signals a breathier, aspirated sound.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㅍ (p): It begins the name of Pyeongchang, the county that hosted the 2018 Winter Olympics.
Korean Hangul consonants, in dictionary.ㅎ (h): It starts the word Hangul itself, which means the Korean script.

Asian capitals from north to south.Astana: Kazakhstan moved its capital here from Almaty in 1997. It was renamed Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022.
Asian capitals from north to south.Ulaanbaatar: It is often called the coldest national capital in the world.
Asian capitals from north to south.Tashkent: It was largely rebuilt after a devastating 1966 earthquake, with help from across the Soviet Union.
Asian capitals from north to south.Beijing: It has hosted both Summer (2008) and Winter (2022) Olympic Games, the first city to do so.
Asian capitals from north to south.Seoul: About half of South Korea's population lives in the greater metropolitan area.
Asian capitals from north to south.Kabul: It sits in a high mountain valley at about 1,800 meters, one of the highest capitals in the world.
Asian capitals from north to south.Kathmandu: The valley holds seven UNESCO World Heritage monument zones.
Asian capitals from north to south.Hanoi: The name means city within the rivers, and it has been a capital for over 1,000 years, since 1010.
Asian capitals from north to south.Bangkok: Its full ceremonial name, 168 letters long, is among the longest place names in the world.
Asian capitals from north to south.Jakarta: The city is sinking, so Indonesia is building a new capital, Nusantara, on Borneo.

When these famous 'lasts' happened.Anna Göldi, the 'last witch': Executed in Switzerland, she was officially pardoned in 2008, more than 220 years later.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Last Holy Roman Emperor quits: Francis II dissolved the empire, which had lasted for nearly a thousand years, after Napoleon's victories.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Pony Express's final run: It ended only months after the telegraph linked the coasts, making the riders obsolete.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Last shogun resigns: Tokugawa Yoshinobu's resignation led to the Meiji Restoration and the end of samurai rule.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Britain's last public hanging: Michael Barrett, a Fenian convicted over the Clerkenwell explosion, was the last man publicly hanged.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Last passenger pigeon dies: Martha, the final one, died at Cincinnati Zoo, once the most numerous bird in North America.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Last tsar abdicates: Nicholas II abdicated and was executed the following year with his family.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Last Model T built: Ford built over 15 million of them from 1908 to 1927.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Last guillotine execution: Hamida Djandoubi was executed in Marseille; France abolished the death penalty four years later.
When these famous 'lasts' happened.Concorde's final flight: It retired after 27 years of flights across the Atlantic in under 3.5 hours.

How long one orbit takes.International Space Station: The ISS circles the Earth about 16 times a day, so astronauts see 16 sunrises every 24 hours.
How long one orbit takes.Phobos around Mars: This tiny moon of Mars orbits so closely that it rises twice a day, and it is slowly spiraling inward.
How long one orbit takes.GPS satellite: Each GPS satellite circles Earth twice a day, and it must account for relativity to stay accurate.
How long one orbit takes.Geostationary satellite: Geostationary satellites orbit above the equator in step with Earth's spin, so they hang above one spot; weather and TV satellites use this.
How long one orbit takes.The Moon around Earth: The Moon takes about 27.3 days to circle the Earth, and the same face always points toward us.
How long one orbit takes.Mercury around the Sun: Mercury's year is shorter than its day on the clock: it takes about 59 Earth days to spin once.
How long one orbit takes.Earth around the Sun: Our year is 365.25 days long, and that quarter day is why we add a leap day.
How long one orbit takes.Jupiter around the Sun: Jupiter's year lasts almost 12 Earth years, and its slow orbit means each zodiac sign hosts it for about a year.
How long one orbit takes.Pluto around the Sun: Pluto was discovered in 1930 and has not yet completed one orbit since then, because it takes about 248 years.
How long one orbit takes.Sun around the Milky Way: Our Sun has circled the galaxy only about 20 times, and the dinosaurs appeared roughly one galactic year ago.

From the coldest place known to the Sun'.Boomerang Nebula: The coldest known place in nature; expanding gas has chilled it to about one degree above absolute zero.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.Cosmic microwave background: This is the faint afterglow of the Big Bang, which fills the entire universe; some old TV static came from it.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.Liquid nitrogen: Doctors use it to freeze off warts, and it is used to preserve biological samples.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.Antarctica's record low: The record was set at Vostok Station in 1983, at about -89 degrees.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.Boiling water: This is true at sea level; on top of Mount Everest, it boils at around 70 degrees.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.Molten lava: Basaltic lava is typically between about 1,000 and 1,200 degrees when it erupts.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.The Sun's surface: Sunlight from it takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.Lightning bolt: A bolt is roughly five times hotter than the Sun's surface, though it lasts only a split second.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.The Sun's corona: It is far hotter than the surface below it, a puzzle called the coronal heating problem; seen during total eclipses.
From the coldest place known to the Sun'.The Sun's core: Hydrogen fuses into helium here, and the energy takes many thousands of years to work its way out.

Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Megalosaurus named: It was named by William Buckland, and it was formally described before the word 'dinosaur' was even coined in 1842.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Iguanodon named: Gideon Mantell named it for its resemblance to iguana teeth, and early reconstructions mistakenly put its thumb spike on its nose.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Neanderthal man: Found in Germany's Neander valley, it was the first extinct human relative recognized, and many people today carry a little of its DNA.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Archaeopteryx: This toothed, feathered creature turned up just after Darwin's Origin of Species, a famous link between dinosaurs and birds.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Java Man: Eugène Dubois found it in Indonesia on purpose, searching for a 'missing link'. It is now classed as Homo erectus.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Tyrannosaurus rex named: Its name means 'tyrant lizard king', and Henry Fairfield Osborn named it from bones found in Montana.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Peking Man skull: The fossils vanished in 1941 while being shipped out of China during wartime and have never been found, so only casts remain.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Lucy: Found in Ethiopia and named after a Beatles song playing in camp, she walked upright about 3.2 million years ago.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.Ötzi the Iceman: Natural freezing preserved his stomach contents, clothes and 61 tattoos, giving a rare glimpse of everyday life in the Copper Age.
Famous fossil and ancient-human finds.The 'Hobbit' (H. floresiensis): Found on the Indonesian island of Flores, adults stood only about 1 m tall, possibly an example of island dwarfism.

Great moments of exploration.Balboa sights the Pacific: Vasco Núñez de Balboa crossed Panama's isthmus and waded into the Pacific, claiming it for Spain; he was later beheaded.
Great moments of exploration.Cortés lands in Mexico: Hernán Cortés began the conquest of the Aztec Empire, helped by indigenous allies and a devastating smallpox epidemic.
Great moments of exploration.Pizarro captures Atahualpa: With about 170 men, Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor, then executed him despite a ransom of gold.
Great moments of exploration.Cartier sails the St. Lawrence: Jacques Cartier's voyages gave Canada its name, from the Iroquoian word 'kanata', meaning village.
Great moments of exploration.Drake sails around the world: Francis Drake's voyage made him a hero, and Elizabeth I knighted him aboard the Golden Hind.
Great moments of exploration.Hudson explores his river: Henry Hudson sailed up the river now bearing his name seeking a route to Asia; mutineers later left him adrift in Hudson Bay.
Great moments of exploration.Tasman reaches Tasmania: Abel Tasman sighted the island he called Van Diemen's Land, later renamed for him, and also sighted New Zealand.
Great moments of exploration.Cook lands at Botany Bay: The bay was named for the many plants collected by botanist Joseph Banks; it began as 'Stingray Harbour'.
Great moments of exploration.Lewis and Clark reach Pacific: Their expedition was guided by Sacagawea, a Shoshone woman who interpreted for them while carrying her infant son.
Great moments of exploration.Livingstone at Victoria Falls: David Livingstone named the falls for his queen; locals call them Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'.

Parts of a web address, left to right.Scheme (protocol): The 's' in 'https' means traffic is encrypted via TLS, whereas plain http is readable by anyone en route.
Parts of a web address, left to right.User credentials: Embedding passwords this way is deprecated, and phishers have used it to disguise addresses.
Parts of a web address, left to right.Subdomain: 'www' is just a convention, not a requirement, and sites can use any subdomain they like.
Parts of a web address, left to right.Domain name: IANA reserves example.com for documentation, so it is safe to use in tutorials.
Parts of a web address, left to right.Top-level domain: The first .com was registered in 1985, and there are now hundreds of other extensions like .app.
Parts of a web address, left to right.Port: Port 8080 is a common alternative for web servers; the default for http is 80 and for https 443.
Parts of a web address, left to right.Path: It echoes the folder structure of old file systems, where pages lived in directories.
Parts of a web address, left to right.File name: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, invented by Tim Berners-Lee around 1990.
Parts of a web address, left to right.Query string: The question mark begins a query, which carries search terms and often tracking tags.
Parts of a web address, left to right.Fragment: The part after # is never sent to the server; the browser uses it to jump to an anchor.

Precious metal purity.US nickel coin (nickel): The coin is not actually nickel alone but about 75 percent copper. Nothing here is precious.
Precious metal purity.9-karat gold: Common in British jewelry because it is affordable, though barely over a third gold.
Precious metal purity.10-karat gold: The minimum purity that can legally be sold as gold in the United States.
Precious metal purity.14-karat gold: Popular for US jewelry, as the added metals make it far tougher than purer gold.
Precious metal purity.18-karat gold: The classic choice for fine jewelry, three parts gold to one part other metal.
Precious metal purity.Coin silver: Silver 90 percent pure with copper was the standard for US coins until 1964.
Precious metal purity.22-karat gold: The traditional gold of Indian jewelry, and used in British sovereign coins. It is soft but rich in color.
Precious metal purity.Sterling silver: Silver mixed with copper for strength. The 'sterling' name's origin is disputed.
Precious metal purity.Britannia silver: Introduced in England in 1697 to discourage the clipping of silver coins.
Precious metal purity.24-karat gold: Pure gold is so soft that you can dent it with your teeth or fingernail.

Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Pan: Only about 20 km wide, Pan orbits inside the Encke Gap of Saturn's rings and sculpts them, earning its nickname 'the ravioli moon'.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Mimas: A giant crater called Herschel gives Mimas a look like the Death Star; the impact nearly shattered the small moon.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Enceladus: Geysers at its south pole spray water ice into space, and that spray feeds Saturn's E ring. It may hide a liquid ocean.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Tethys: Nearly half-covered by a huge canyon called Ithaca Chasma, Tethys is made almost entirely of water ice.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Dione: Cassini found evidence of a thin oxygen atmosphere here, and bright 'wispy' streaks turned out to be icy cliffs.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Rhea: Saturn's second-largest moon is mostly water ice with a heavily cratered face, and it is about 1,500 km across.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Titan: The only moon with a thick atmosphere, Titan has methane lakes and rain. The Huygens probe landed on it in 2005.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Hyperion: Hyperion looks like a sponge, and it tumbles chaotically instead of spinning steadily, so its day has no fixed length.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Iapetus: One hemisphere is dark and the other bright, and a ridge of mountains circles its equator like a walnut seam.
Saturn's moons by distance from Saturn.Phoebe: Phoebe orbits backward, opposite to most of Saturn's moons, which suggests it's a captured object from the outer solar system.

New Testament books, in Bible order.Mark: The shortest Gospel, and probably the earliest written, it's the source Matthew and Luke drew on for their own accounts.
New Testament books, in Bible order.Luke: Tradition names a physician, Luke, Paul's travel companion, as author, who also wrote the Acts of the Apostles.
New Testament books, in Bible order.Romans: Paul's letter to the Christians of Rome, written from Corinth, is among his longest and most influential.
New Testament books, in Bible order.1 Corinthians: Paul's letters to Corinth deal with a quarrelsome church, and contain the famous passage 'love is patient, love is kind'.
New Testament books, in Bible order.Galatians: Paul wrote to churches in Galatia, in what is now Turkey, arguing that faith, not following the Jewish law, brings salvation.
New Testament books, in Bible order.Ephesians: Paul's letter to the church at Ephesus, a great port city, which was home to the Temple of Artemis, a wonder of the ancient world.
New Testament books, in Bible order.Philippians: Paul wrote this letter from prison, and it's known for its warm, joyful tone, despite the circumstances.
New Testament books, in Bible order.Hebrews: Its author is unknown, though tradition once credited Paul, and it contains the famous definition of faith.
New Testament books, in Bible order.James: Traditionally attributed to a brother of Jesus, this practical letter says faith without works is dead.
New Testament books, in Bible order.Jude: A one-chapter letter that quotes the Book of Enoch, making it one of the shortest books in the New Testament.

When these sandwich chains were founded.Jersey Mike's: Started in 1956 as a Point Pleasant, New Jersey sub shop, it was bought by 17-year-old Peter Cancro in 1971 and grew nationwide.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Arby's: Brothers Forrest and Leroy Raffel named it after their initials, R.B., and the chain is famous for its roast beef sandwiches.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Subway: Fred DeLuca, then 17, borrowed 1,000 dollars from family friend Peter Buck to start it, and it became a huge restaurant chain.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Schlotzsky's: Founded in Austin, Texas, its signature sandwich, the Original, is served on a sourdough-style bun, and the chain started as a small deli.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Potbelly: It began in a Chicago antique shop, and the name refers to the potbelly stove that warmed the sandwich-hungry browsers.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Quiznos: This Denver chain built its name on toasting subs in an oven, which made its sandwiches warm and crunchy.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Jimmy John's: Founded by 19-year-old Jimmy John Liautaud, who borrowed money from his father, it promises 'freaky fast' delivery.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Panera Bread: The bakery-cafe chain started in Missouri as the St. Louis Bread Company, and that name stayed on many local stores for years.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Firehouse Subs: Founded by two brothers who were firefighters, the chain donates millions to first responders through its foundation.
When these sandwich chains were founded.Which Wich: Its name plays on a question, 'which wich?', and it's a Dallas, Texas chain whose bags are written on with markers.

Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Hypatia: Hypatia taught philosophy and mathematics in Alexandria and was killed by a mob in 415 AD; little of her own writing survives.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Maria Sibylla Merian: Merian traveled to Suriname to paint insect life stages, and her detailed metamorphosis illustrations were groundbreaking for natural history.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Émilie du Châtelet: This French polymath translated Newton's Principia into French, and her version remains the standard one in France today.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Florence Nightingale: Nightingale was also a pioneering statistician who invented a pie-chart variant, the polar area diagram, to show how disease killed soldiers.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Marie Curie: Curie remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, Physics in 1903 and Chemistry in 1911.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Barbara McClintock: McClintock discovered 'jumping genes' in maize, work so far ahead of its time that she waited decades before winning the 1983 Nobel Prize.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Rachel Carson: Her 1962 book Silent Spring exposed the harm of pesticides like DDT and helped launch the modern environmental movement.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Dorothy Hodgkin: Hodgkin mapped the structures of penicillin and vitamin B12 with X-ray crystallography and won the 1964 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Rosalind Franklin: Her X-ray image known as Photo 51 gave key evidence of DNA's double helix, but she died in 1958 before the 1962 Nobel Prize went to others.
Pioneering women of science, by birth ye.Jane Goodall: Goodall went into the Tanzanian forest in 1960 with no degree and observed chimpanzees making and using tools, reshaping what we think makes us human.

How long these monarchs reigned.Harold II of England: Harold's short reign ended at Hastings in 1066 with the Norman invasion, after he'd already beaten a Viking army days earlier at Stamford Bridge.
How long these monarchs reigned.Caligula: Gaius Caesar's nickname means 'little boots', and he ruled Rome from 37 to 41 AD before being assassinated by his own guards.
How long these monarchs reigned.Richard the Lionheart: He spent only about six months of his reign actually in England, leading the Third Crusade and being held for ransom on his way home.
How long these monarchs reigned.Alexander the Great: Alexander built an empire stretching from Greece to India in about a decade, then died in Babylon at around age 32.
How long these monarchs reigned.Hadrian: Hadrian built a wall across northern Britain and rebuilt the Pantheon in Rome, traveling the empire for much of his reign.
How long these monarchs reigned.Constantine the Great: He legalized Christianity in the Roman Empire and founded Constantinople, later Istanbul, as his new capital.
How long these monarchs reigned.Augustus: Born Octavian, he became Rome's first emperor and ended decades of civil war, and the month August is named for him.
How long these monarchs reigned.Edward III of England: His reign saw the start of the Hundred Years' War and the Black Death, and he founded the Order of the Garter.
How long these monarchs reigned.Henry III of England: He became king at nine and ruled 56 years, one of England's longest reigns, and rebuilt Westminster Abbey in the Gothic style.
How long these monarchs reigned.Ramesses II: Ramesses II built Abu Simbel and reportedly fathered more than 100 children, and he lived to about 90, outliving many of his heirs.

Windows versions by release.Windows 1.0: Windows 1.0 was a graphical add-on to MS-DOS, and its windows could only be tiled, not overlap.
Windows versions by release.Windows 3.0: Windows 3.0 made PCs truly mainstream with better graphics and Solitaire, which taught people to use a mouse.
Windows versions by release.Windows 95: Windows 95 introduced the Start button and taskbar, and its launch was marketed with Rolling Stones music.
Windows versions by release.Windows 98: Windows 98 added USB support and built internet features into the desktop, and its launch demo famously crashed.
Windows versions by release.Windows XP: Windows XP was one of the longest-lived versions, and the green Start button and Bliss hill wallpaper became iconic.
Windows versions by release.Windows Vista: Vista was criticized for its heavy demands and annoying security prompts, and it was a flop compared to its predecessor.
Windows versions by release.Windows 7: Windows 7 is remembered fondly as a refined version of Vista, and was widely adopted by users.
Windows versions by release.Windows 8: Windows 8 removed the Start button for a touch-focused tile interface, and Microsoft brought it back in 8.1.
Windows versions by release.Windows 10: Windows 10 was called the last version of Windows, and it was free to upgrade for the first year.
Windows versions by release.Windows 11: Windows 11 requires newer hardware, including a security chip called TPM 2.0, and introduced a centered taskbar.

Disney animated classics (no princesses!.Bambi: Bambi's mother's death was a shock for audiences, and animators studied real deer at the studio for realism.
Disney animated classics (no princesses!.Peter Pan: Peter Pan was voiced by Bobby Driscoll, the first Disney film to use a boy actor to portray the title role, and reference footage of dancers helped animators.
Disney animated classics (no princesses!.Lady and the Tramp: The spaghetti scene in Lady and the Tramp was not in the first plan, and Walt Disney was doubtful about it.
Disney animated classics (no princesses!.101 Dalmatians: One Hundred and One Dalmatians used a Xerox process to copy drawings directly onto cels, saving enormous time.
Disney animated classics (no princesses!.The Jungle Book: The Jungle Book was the last animated film Walt Disney personally supervised, as he died during its production.
Disney animated classics (no princesses!.Robin Hood: Robin Hood cast animals in all roles, and the film reused animation from other Disney films to save money.
Disney animated classics (no princesses!.The Lion King: The Lion King was loosely inspired by Hamlet, and its Circle of Life opening is among the best-known in animation.
Disney animated classics (no princesses!.Lilo & Stitch: Lilo and Stitch was set in Hawaii, and Chris Sanders designed Stitch from a sketch he made years earlier for a children's book.
Disney animated classics (no princesses!.Zootopia: Zootopia was built on a world of mammals with different sizes, and its sloth DMV scene became a famous joke.

Famous pitches from lowest to highest.32-foot organ pipe C: This pitch is so low you'd feel it more than hear it, and the largest organ pipes make notes below the range of human hearing.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.Lowest key on a piano: The piano's lowest key is A0, and a standard piano has 88 keys, spanning more than seven octaves.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.Bass guitar's low E: A bass guitar's lowest string is tuned to the same notes as the double bass, and it is an octave below the guitar.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.Guitar's low E: Guitar's low E is the thickest string, and tuners can use it to check every other string's tuning.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.Violin's lowest G: The violin's lowest string is G, and the instrument's four strings are tuned in perfect fifths.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.Middle C: Middle C sits near the center of the piano keyboard, and it is the note where the treble and bass staves meet.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.Concert A (orchestra tuning): The orchestra tunes to the oboe's A at 440 Hz, though some orchestras tune slightly higher, to 442 or more.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.Queen of the Night's top F: Mozart wrote the Queen of the Night's aria in The Magic Flute with two high Fs, and it's among the most difficult in opera.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.A flute's standard top C: The flute's top range is piercing, and a piccolo plays an octave higher, making it the highest instrument in the orchestra.
Famous pitches from lowest to highest.Highest key on a piano: The piano's highest note, C8, is very high-pitched, and it sits nearly at the upper limit of what most instruments can produce.

Christmas movies and specials by release.It's a Wonderful Life: It flopped at first, and became a classic after its copyright lapsed and TV stations replayed it every December.
Christmas movies and specials by release.Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer: The Rankin/Bass stop-motion special is the longest-running Christmas special on TV; the character was created by Robert L. May for a store in 1939.
Christmas movies and specials by release.A Charlie Brown Christmas: Network executives disliked its jazz soundtrack by Vince Guaraldi, but the music became its heart.
Christmas movies and specials by release.A Christmas Story: Ralphie's quest for a Red Ryder BB gun, and that leg-lamp, made it a TV staple, with marathons every year.
Christmas movies and specials by release.Die Hard: The action takes place at a Christmas Eve party, and the film is based on a novel called Nothing Lasts Forever.
Christmas movies and specials by release.Christmas Vacation: The Griswolds' lights-heavy holiday is based on a John Hughes short story, and Chevy Chase starred.
Christmas movies and specials by release.Home Alone: It made a star of Macaulay Culkin, and grossed over $400 million worldwide.
Christmas movies and specials by release.The Nightmare Before Christmas: Tim Burton wrote the original poem, and director Henry Selick spent years animating it frame by frame.
Christmas movies and specials by release.Elf: Buddy the human elf famously puts maple syrup on his spaghetti, and the film was shot on location in New York.
Christmas movies and specials by release.Klaus: Spanish animator Sergio Pablos made this hand-drawn Netflix film, which earned an Oscar nomination.

Oldest known individuals.Flopsy (rabbit): Likely the oldest rabbit on record, she lived in Tasmania; pet rabbits typically live around 8 to 12 years.
Oldest known individuals.Bluey (cattle dog): An Australian cattle dog who worked on farms in Victoria; his 29 years and 5 months is the longest verified dog life.
Oldest known individuals.Creme Puff (cat): This Texas cat lived over 38 years, more than four times a typical cat's lifespan, in the care of Jake Perry.
Oldest known individuals.Tish (goldfish): Won at a fairground in 1956 and lived 43 years in a Yorkshire home, far longer than the few years most goldfish manage.
Oldest known individuals.Old Billy (horse): A barge horse born in 1760 in England, he reached 62; his skull is kept at the Manchester Museum.
Oldest known individuals.Lin Wang (elephant): An Asian elephant who worked for the Chinese army, then lived in Taiwan; he died at Taipei Zoo in 2003.
Oldest known individuals.Jeanne Calment (human): She met Vincent van Gogh as a girl in Arles; she died in 1997 as the longest verified human lifespan.
Oldest known individuals.Bowhead whale (estimate): Old harpoon fragments found in living Arctic whales helped reveal that they can outlive nearly any other mammal.
Oldest known individuals.Greenland shark (estimate): It grows about a centimeter a year and doesn't mature until around 150, making it the longest-lived vertebrate known.
Oldest known individuals.Ming the ocean quahog clam: Dredged up off Iceland in 2006 and dated by counting shell growth rings, it died in the process; a record for any animal.

Batteries by weight.CR2032 coin cell: The name encodes size: 20 mm wide, 3.2 mm thick, which is why these coin cells are easily swallowed by small children.
Batteries by weight.AAA battery: Its alkaline cells give 1.5 volts like larger AAs, but hold less than half the energy.
Batteries by weight.AA battery: In Germany it's the 'Mignon', and its official code is LR6.
Batteries by weight.Rectangular 9-volt: Pry it open and you find six tiny cells stacked in a row inside.
Batteries by weight.C battery: Once standard in toys and flashlights, it sits in size between AA and D.
Batteries by weight.D battery: Though it has the same 1.5 volts as an AAA, it stores about ten times as much energy.
Batteries by weight.6-volt lantern battery: The spring-top battery powers camping lanterns and electric fences.
Batteries by weight.E-bike battery: A typical pack holds roughly half a kilowatt-hour, enough for many miles of assisted riding.
Batteries by weight.Car starter battery: Lead-acid chemistry, invented by Gaston Planté in 1859, is still what starts most cars today.
Batteries by weight.Tesla Model 3 battery pack: The pack is made of thousands of small cylindrical cells wired together.

Counting words.Pair: Two of anything. Odd quirk: we also call single items like scissors and trousers 'a pair', though they are one object.
Counting words.Half dozen: Egg cartons of six are common. Twelve and its halves stuck around because they divide so neatly.
Counting words.Dozen: Twelve has more divisors than ten, and some mathematicians still argue base twelve would have been a better counting system.
Counting words.Baker's dozen: Medieval English bakers faced harsh penalties for selling short-weight loaves, so they supposedly tossed in a thirteenth to be safe.
Counting words.Score: Lincoln's 'Four score and seven years ago' means 87. The word comes from counting sheep by notches, or scores, cut in a stick.
Counting words.Quire of paper: Bookbinders stitch quires together into books. In the old paper trade, twenty quires made up a ream.
Counting words.Gross: Twelve dozen, long a wholesaler's unit for items like pencils and buttons. 'Gross' comes from Old French for 'large'.
Counting words.Ream of paper: Office paper still comes in 500-sheet reams. The word traces back to Arabic 'rizma', meaning a bundle.
Counting words.Great gross: A dozen gross, or twelve cubed. No shopper buys it, but it is genuine wholesaler's vocabulary.
Counting words.Myriad: From the Greek for 10,000, it was the biggest number ancient Greek had a single word for. Today it just means 'countless'.

When these composers were born.Antonio Vivaldi: Vivaldi taught music to orphaned girls in Venice, and wrote many concertos for them. His Four Seasons paints weather and birdsong in sound.
When these composers were born.Joseph Haydn: The "father of the symphony" wrote over 100 of them. He also taught Beethoven, and was friends with Mozart.
When these composers were born.Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart: A child prodigy who played for royalty, he died at 35. He left his Requiem unfinished.
When these composers were born.Ludwig van Beethoven: He kept composing after losing his hearing. His Ninth Symphony, with its choral finale, was written when he was almost completely deaf.
When these composers were born.Franz Schubert: Schubert died at 31 but wrote over 600 songs, plus symphonies. His Unfinished Symphony has just two movements.
When these composers were born.Frédéric Chopin: The Polish composer wrote almost entirely for piano. When he died in Paris his heart was sent back to Warsaw.
When these composers were born.Giuseppe Verdi: His operas like La traviata and Aida are core of the repertory. During Italy's unification, crowds shouted "Viva VERDI" as a patriotic code.
When these composers were born.Johannes Brahms: He worked on his first symphony for over twenty years, afraid of being compared with Beethoven. His lullaby is known worldwide.
When these composers were born.Pyotr Tchaikovsky: The composer of Swan Lake and The Nutcracker also wrote the 1812 Overture, which famously calls for cannon fire.
When these composers were born.Claude Debussy: Clair de Lune's composer pioneered a shimmering, impressionistic sound, though he disliked that label. He was inspired by Javanese gamelan.

Health advice, ranked by the number in i.Minutes to brush your teeth: Most people brush for well under a minute, so electric brushes build in a two-minute timer to correct that.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.Daily fruit and veg portions: The '5 a day' slogan began in California in 1988, and WHO later set a target of at least 400 grams.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.Minimum hours of adult sleep: Teenagers need more, about eight to ten hours, and regular short sleepers often underestimate their impairment.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.Glasses of water a day: The 'eight glasses' rule has little firm science behind it; needs vary, and food provides water too.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.UK weekly alcohol unit limit: A UK unit is 10 ml of pure alcohol, so 14 units is about six pints of average-strength beer.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.Seconds to wash your hands: Roughly the time it takes to hum 'Happy Birthday' twice.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.WHO daily sugar limit (g): WHO suggests under 10 percent of energy from free sugars, and 5 percent, about 25 g, for added benefit.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.Weekly minutes of exercise: A brisk walk counts as moderate exercise, so a half-hour walk on five days meets this.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.Daily calories on food labels: This is a round reference figure printed on labels, not a personal target.
Health advice, ranked by the number in i.Daily step goal: The figure traces to a 1960s Japanese pedometer marketing campaign called manpo-kei, 'ten-thousand-step meter'.

An oak's life, acorn to log.Acorn drops from an oak: An oak may only drop a large crop of acorns every few years, which overwhelms the animals that eat them. That is called masting.
An oak's life, acorn to log.Squirrel buries it: Squirrels bury thousands of acorns but forget many, so they accidentally plant new oak woods. Jays also hide acorns this way.
An oak's life, acorn to log.Root pushes out: The first thing to emerge is a taproot, which anchors the seedling and goes down. Oaks establish a deep root before sending up a shoot.
An oak's life, acorn to log.Shoot breaks the soil: The young shoot is pale and delicate at first, and vulnerable to browsing deer, rabbits and mice, so few acorns survive to this stage.
An oak's life, acorn to log.First leaves unfold: The first true leaves are lobed and bright green. The seedling lives on food stored in the acorn until its leaves can make enough energy.
An oak's life, acorn to log.Grows into a sapling: Saplings grow slowly in shade. Oaks are long-lived trees and may take decades to grow into proper trees.
An oak's life, acorn to log.Makes its first acorns: An oak may not bear acorns until it is 20 to 50 years old. Even then, only occasionally good years produce a heavy crop.
An oak's life, acorn to log.Becomes a mighty old oak: Some oaks live for 500 years or more, and a few for over a thousand. A single mature oak can support hundreds of species of insects and other life.
An oak's life, acorn to log.Falls in a storm: Even after falling, an old oak can sprout from its roots or branches. Its timber was prized for building ships, such as Nelson's Victory.
An oak's life, acorn to log.Rots back into the soil: Dead oak wood feeds fungi, beetles and many other creatures for decades. A rotting log is a whole ecosystem and returns nutrients to the soil.

Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Egyptian embalming use: Cinnamon was so rare in ancient Egypt that it was used in embalming and temple offerings.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Nero burns cinnamon: Legend says Nero burned a year's supply of Rome's cinnamon at the funeral of his wife Poppaea.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Da Gama reaches India: Vasco da Gama's sea route to India opened the way for the Portuguese spice trade.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Portuguese reach Ceylon: They built a fort in Colombo, seeking a monopoly on cinnamon.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Dutch take Galle: The Dutch East India Company seized Galle and took the cinnamon trade from the Portuguese.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.British take Ceylon: Britain's capture of Dutch Ceylon ended the Dutch monopoly, and cinnamon was later grown elsewhere.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Sri Lanka independence: Ceylon became independent in 1948, and is known for true cinnamon, Cinnamomum verum, unlike cheaper cassia.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Cinnamon Toast Crunch: Its sugar-and-cinnamon-coated squares have a cult following, and General Mills makes it.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Cinnabon founded: The first Cinnabon opened in a Seattle mall, and its stores bake in view to spread the aroma.
Cinnamon, from pharaohs to Cinnabon.Swedish Cinnamon Bun Day: Sweden's Kanelbullens Dag falls on October 4, started by the Home Baking Council.

Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.Hello, Dolly!: Louis Armstrong's recording knocked The Beatles from number one in 1964.
Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.Hello, Goodbye: The Beatles song written by Paul McCartney, built on contrasts like yes and no, hit number one.
Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.First \"Hello, World\" program: Brian Kernighan used it in a Bell Labs tutorial for the B language, and it became the traditional first program.
Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.World Hello Day: It was created in response to the Egypt-Israel war, and people are asked to greet ten others.
Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.Hello Kitty: Created at Sanrio, she is officially a British schoolgirl named Kitty White from suburban London, with no mouth.
Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.Lionel Richie's Hello: Its video features him as a teacher falling for a blind student, who sculpts a clay head.
Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.Hello! magazine: Founded in Spain as Hola!, the British edition launched in 1988 and is famed for celebrity weddings.
Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.HelloFresh: The Berlin-based meal-kit company later became one of the largest in the world.
Famous \"Hello\"s, by year.Adele's Hello: Its video was viewed over 27 million times on its first day, a record at the time.
